G L E U H R
Wellness Pvt Ltd  ·  Aesthetic Medicine
Front Desk Reception — Assessment Test
Post-training readiness assessment · Total 60 marks · Pass ≥ 80% (48)
Candidate Name

Branch / Outlet

Date

Assessor

Score
      / 60
Result
Pass / Fail
Instructions: Answer all questions. Parts A–D are written by the candidate; Part E is a practical role-play observed and scored by the assessor. Write clearly. No mobile phones or notes.
  PART A — Multiple Choice  (10 × 1 = 10 marks)   ·   Circle the correct option
Q1.  Within how many seconds should a client be greeted on walking in?[1]
A)  15            B)  5            C)  10            D)  2    
Q2.  When locating an appointment, you should find it by the client's:[1]
A)  Phone number            B)  Name            C)  Token number            D)  ID card    
Q3.  Which of these is an absolute red line at the desk?[1]
A)  Rescheduling            B)  Off-system / cash-in-hand payment            C)  Offering water            D)  Sending a WhatsApp receipt    
Q4.  A clinical question from a client should be:[1]
A)  Answered by reception            B)  Routed to the doctor via the FDM            C)  Ignored            D)  Answered from the internet    
Q5.  If a client starts shouting in the waiting area, you first:[1]
A)  Argue back            B)  Move them to a private cabin            C)  Call police at once            D)  Offer a refund    
Q6.  In feedback ratings out of 5, which counts as a concern (DSAT)?[1]
A)  5            B)  4            C)  3            D)  None    
Q7.  For treatment staff, the only permitted jewellery is:[1]
A)  Bangles            B)  Stud earrings            C)  Rings            D)  A watch    
Q8.  Before collecting any payment, you must first:[1]
A)  Say thank you            B)  State the amount and purpose            C)  Ask for a tip            D)  Take a photo    
Q9.  If police visit the clinic, you should:[1]
A)  Admit fault            B)  Inform Head Office/senior management immediately and let them coordinate            C)  Sign their documents            D)  Argue the case    
Q10.  The three affirmations are used at:[1]
A)  Welcome, the wait, and the goodbye            B)  Only at billing            C)  Only on the phone            D)  At lunch    
  PART B — True or False  (8 × 1 = 8 marks)   ·   Circle one
Q1.  You may leave the front desk unattended if you are very busy.[1]
True   /   False
Q2.  A personal phone may be used at the desk in front of clients.[1]
True   /   False
Q3.  Every enquiry must be logged — no lead is ever lost.[1]
True   /   False
Q4.  It is acceptable to argue with a client to defend the clinic.[1]
True   /   False
Q5.  A WhatsApp receipt must be sent for every payment.[1]
True   /   False
Q6.  Reception may advise a client on post-care after a treatment.[1]
True   /   False
Q7.  Tomorrow's appointment confirmations are sent the evening before.[1]
True   /   False
Q8.  Under pressure from police, agreeing to a refund on the spot is fine.[1]
True   /   False
  PART C — Complete / Short Answer  (6 × 2 = 12 marks)
Q1.  Complete the Welcome affirmation:  “Welcome to GLEUHR. ______________________.”[1]

Q2.  Complete the line for a police visit:  “We follow standard medical protocols with proper consent and documentation. ______________________.”[1]

Q3.  The four escalation principles are:  Stay calm,  ______________,  ______________,  Escalate early.[1]

Q4.  In CSAT, ratings ____ and ____ = Satisfied; ratings ____, ____ and ____ = Dissatisfied.[1]

Q5.  Name any THREE of the six Reception KRAs.[2]


Q6.  List the five steps of the L.E.A.R.N. objection-handling method.[2]


  PART D — Scenario Questions  (5 × 4 = 20 marks)
Q1.  A client says: “It's too expensive.” Write how you would respond (mention your approach and a sample line).[4]



Q2.  A first-time client walks in looking nervous. Describe what you do in the first few seconds and how you settle her before her consultation.[4]



Q3.  A client is unhappy about her results and starts getting loud in the waiting area. List the steps you take, in order.[4]



Q4.  It is opening time. List five things you check/confirm before the first client is allowed in.[4]



Q5.  A client demands a discount you are not authorised to give. Explain how you handle it without losing the client.[4]



  PART E — Practical Role-Play  (Observed by assessor · 10 marks)
The candidate runs a short live/role-play front-desk scenario. Assessor scores each item 0 (not shown) / 1 (partly) / 2 (fully).
#
Observed behaviour
Score (0–2)
1
Greets within 10 seconds — by name, with a warm smile

2
Locates the appointment by name; checks the client in smoothly

3
Offers hospitality (water/tea) and communicates any wait

4
Handles a phone call without ignoring the client in front of her

5
Bills transparently — states amount & purpose; mentions the WhatsApp receipt

6
Grooming & desk to standard; confident, professional demeanour

7
Warm goodbye — walks the client out, uses her name

Result:  Pass ≥ 48 / 60 (80%).   Below 80% → re-training on weak areas and re-test. Candidate signature: ____________   Assessor signature: ____________

  ANSWER KEY & MARKING SCHEME — FOR ASSESSOR ONLY
Part A (1 mark each):  1-B · 2-B · 3-B · 4-B · 5-B · 6-C · 7-B · 8-B · 9-B · 10-A
Part B (1 mark each):  1-False · 2-False · 3-True · 4-False · 5-True · 6-False · 7-True · 8-False
Part C (marking guide):
1. “…Please come in.”
2. “…Our management team will coordinate with you.”
3. Do not argue · Do not commit.
4. 4 and 5 = Satisfied · 1, 2 and 3 = Dissatisfied.
5. Any three of: Greeting & Client Experience · Appointment Management · Call & Message Handling · Billing Accuracy & Transparency · Records & CRM Hygiene · Front Desk Discipline & Brand Stewardship.
6. Listen · Empathise · Ask · Respond (with value) · Next step.
Part D (4 marks each — award for key points):
1. Acknowledge/empathise; shift to value & safety (not price); offer EMI/package; give a next step. Sample line accepted.
2. Be on her side of the desk, greet warmly in seconds by name; welcome affirmation; offer to seat/hospitality; orient her calmly before the consult; don't hover while she fills the form.
3. Move to a private cabin; don't argue in front of others; offer water & listen; ensure 2 staff present; do NOT admit fault or commit a refund; inform Head Office/FDM; follow the Escalation Matrix; ensure safety.
4. Any five: schedule reviewed & dashboard open; systems/CRM/billing/phone live; desk & float ready; reception, washrooms & water station confirmed ready with housekeeping; clinical rooms/sterile stock ready; staff groomed; final walkthrough.
5. Don't argue or commit; hold the price and offer package value; route to Counsellor/FDM for any approved offer; keep it warm; secure a next step and log the lead.
Part E:  Sum the 7 items (max 14) and scale to 10 (score ÷ 14 × 10).
Overall: 48/60 (80%) to pass. Below that, coach the weak part(s) and re-test per the Training Framework sign-off.
